evals.prompt: I have a Jetpack Compose CartScreen backed by a CartViewModel. Add analytics so that opening the cart records a screen view exactly once, and tapping the checkout button records a click. Show the Kotlin code.
assertions: The screen-view tracking call is placed in the ViewModel (e.g. its init block or load function), NOT inside the composable body or a LaunchedEffect(Unit)
The checkout tracking is triggered from a ViewModel handler that the composable invokes via a hoisted intent callback (e.g. onCheckoutClicked), with the composable never calling the tracker directly

evals.prompt: Our cart screen is under two A/B experiments at once: checkout_layout (compact vs full) and price_badge (control vs variant_b). When the screen is viewed, record which variant of each experiment the user is in for analytics. Write the Kotlin.
assertions: A single screen-view call carries all active experiments together (e.g. trackScreenWithExperiments passing a list of Experiment(key, value)), rather than branching the tracking call per variant with if/when
The code does not emit a separately named event per experiment variant

evals.prompt: In our LoginViewModel, after a successful login I want to send a login analytics event that ties the event to the user (they have an email and a customer id). Write the tracking code, including how consent is handled.
assertions: Raw PII (the user's email and/or customer id) is NOT placed directly in event parameters; the identifier is hashed (e.g. SHA-256) or omitted

Consent is enforced centrally in the tracker/implementation layer (anonymizing or nullifying identifiers when analytics consent is withheld) rather than the ViewModel/feature code checking consent before each call

evals.prompt: Write a JVM unit test verifying that CartViewModel.onCheckoutClicked() records the checkout click for analytics, and that nothing is tracked before the user taps.
assertions: The test injects an in-memory fake implementation of the tracker interface rather than the real analytics SDK or a Mockito/mock verify on a string name
It asserts the exact typed event by equality (e.g. ButtonClickEvent with uniqueName "cart_checkout"), not a string substring or a call count alone
